evidence.reviewer_ensemble: builder pass, skeptic pass, taste pass — see the reviewer_ensemble object.
evidence.reviewer_disagreement_reviewed: The skeptic's objection is that this changes nothing today, since `User-agent: *  Allow: /` already permits every one of these agents, so calling it a GEO win would overstate it. Accepted rather than argued down: the PR body and the code comment both state plainly that it is a durable declaration, not an unblock. It is retained on two narrower grounds — several engines document honouring their own named directive ahead of the wildcard, and a future narrowing of `*` would silently revoke access that named rules would preserve.
evidence.winner_rationale: Declaring the agents by name is cheap, reversible, matches what flas/geebs/titanforge already do, and removes a real inconsistency in the portfolio. The alternative considered and rejected was adding Disallow rules or crawl-delay, which would risk reducing access on a site whose declared bottleneck is audience.

builder.evidence: app/robots.ts moves from a single rule object to a rules array: the existing wildcard rule is preserved verbatim and seven named AI agents are appended. absoluteUrl() and both sitemap entries are unchanged. Generated output confirmed from .next/server/app/robots.txt.body.

skeptic.evidence: The gap was measured, not assumed: robots.txt was fetched live for all six portfolio domains with redirects followed, and esteban returned 4 lines with zero AI-crawler directives while flas, geebs and titanforge each named all four majors. An earlier pass of this same audit was WRONG — it hit the apex domain, which 301s to www, and so graded several sites against a redirect stub; the audit was re-run with -L and the corrected table is what this PR cites. The claim is deliberately limited to 'declaration', not 'unblock', because the wildcard already allows these agents.

taste.evidence: Agent list is a named const with one-line comments explaining what each crawler is for, and a block comment recording the audit that motivated it, so a future reader does not delete it as redundant with the wildcard.

reviewer_disagreement_reviewed: Skeptic held that this is a no-op today. Accepted and stated plainly in the PR body and code comment rather than overstated; retained for the named-directive precedence and future-narrowing arguments.
winner_rationale: A cheap, reversible declaration that closes a measured inconsistency across the portfolio, on the one brand where crawl access is on the critical path for its declared audience bottleneck.
